analysis: What changed versus the 7 AM PT brief: (1) No bounce — 90 minutes into the session the CPI repricing is holding: S&P 500 -0.6% to -0.8%, Nasdaq -0.8% to -0.9%, Dow flat to -0.1%; 10Y 5.26% in recent trading, off its 5.33% post-CPI high; October hike odds steady at ~44% (CME FedWatch). The market has accepted the coin-flip hike as base case rather than fading it. (2) The tape's composition matters: healthcare (+1.8%) and staples (+0.8%) are masking tech pain in the Dow while 7 of 11 S&P sectors fall, so index reads flatter than the actual pain. (3) Bowman offered the first dovish-leaning Fed voice since the print, but the tape didn't bite — dovish words are losing to hot data until Thursday's PPI lands. (4) The AI-capex anxiety met its first real demand data: ASML's record quarter, third guide raise this year, and '30% expansions in 2027 and 2028 will not meet demand' — and semis sold off anyway (SOXX -2.5%, memory ETF -2.5%). Fundamentals lost to positioning. (5) Earnings-wave dispersion is now a sector move: the S&P 500 Banks index at a 4-month low on BAC (-8.5%) and MS (-2.5% to -3.4% despite the beat), while BlackRock's beat halved to +2%. Correction carried: ASML reported Wednesday, not Thursday — it belongs to today's brief, not tomorrow's watch list. Earnings context carried: BAC Q3 adjusted EPS $1.08 vs $1.10 on the $1.2B AML fine; MS $3.03 vs $2.93; BLK $15.93 vs $14.32 on $15.49T AUM; ASML Q3 EPS $14.89 vs $12.17, sales EUR 11.7B, 2026 guide raised to EUR 44-45B. Signal vs noise: CPI numbers confirmed across outlets; bank prints confirmed; ASML confirmed across outlets; Bowman single-source (Barchart reporting her IIF speech); the CXMT 4F2 claim remains unverified; October hike odds disagree by tracker (43.7-44% CME vs 54% one tracker) — treat the exact number as approximate. Community: nothing qualified — the Stocktwits CPI poll thread is pre-print political chatter; HN has no fresh thread on today's print or ASML; Reddit searches returned nothing qualifying.

headlines.headline: Mid-morning tape: the CPI repricing is holding, not fading — S&P 500 -0.6% to -0.8%, Nasdaq -0.8% to -0.9%, Dow flat to -0.1%. Healthcare (+1.8%) and staples (+0.8%) cushioned the Dow while 7 of 11 S&P sectors fell. October hike odds steady at ~44% (CME FedWatch, up from 22% Tuesday); 10Y at 5.26% in recent trading, off its 5.33% post-CPI high.
headlines.why_it_matters: The open didn't bounce — the market is pricing the coin-flip October hike as the base case now, not a headline overreaction to fade.

headlines.headline: Fed Vice Chair Michelle Bowman signaled she favors keeping policy steady at the October FOMC meeting: 'We have some time to wait and see how financial conditions and the economy evolve before we decide that we need to take any more action' — giving stocks and bonds some support this morning.
headlines.why_it_matters: One dovish-leaning voice caps the hawkish repricing — but it's a single report of her IIF-speech remarks, and she may be outvoted at the Oct 28 meeting if Thursday's PPI confirms the CPI.

headlines.headline: Bank wave deepens: Bank of America down ~8.5% (WSJ: profit disappointed even excluding the $1.2B fine), Morgan Stanley down 2.5-3.4% despite its EPS beat; the S&P 500 Banks index fell 2.4% to its lowest in 4+ months. BlackRock +2%, halved from its +5% premarket peak.
headlines.why_it_matters: Bank earnings are trading on their merits in a market that has moved on — BAC is being priced on governance risk, not the fine's math; a rate-fear tape doesn't reward beats.

headlines.headline: ASML reported Q3 Wednesday: record EUR 11.7B sales (vs EUR 7.52B a year ago), EPS $14.89 vs $12.17 expected, though revenue hairline-missed (EUR 11.66B vs EUR 11.71B Visible Alpha). 2026 outlook raised to EUR 44-45B — the third raise this year; Q4 guide EUR 14.2-15.2B; 57.5% gross margin. CEO Fouquet: the planned 30% capacity expansions in 2027 and 2028 'will not allow us to meet our customer demand'; customers expect chip supply below demand through 2028, with orders extending to 2029-2030. US-listed shares edged lower anyway.
headlines.why_it_matters: The strongest AI-demand signal of the week is being sold anyway — semis are trading on positioning and valuation, not order books.

headlines.headline: Memory selloff extends to a third straight session despite ASML's record demand read: the Roundhill Memory ETF (DRAM) -2.5%, SOXX -2.5%; Micron, Sandisk, SK Hynix, Seagate and Western Digital all red. The CXMT 4F2 claim remains unverified.
headlines.why_it_matters: Memory is trading on the CXMT fear, not the HBM reality — ASML's demand boom failing to lift the group says the tape doesn't believe this selloff is about demand.

headlines.headline: Tesla down 1.8% to $368.62 after Uber's autonomous mobility president Sarfraz Maredia announced he is leaving Uber after November 16 to take a role 'outside of the AV ecosystem'; Uber -0.4% in early trading.
headlines.why_it_matters: Personnel moves in the robo-taxi race are moving the stock more than the Roadster livestream 24 hours away — the self-driving premium is fragile to competitive narrative shifts.

headlines.headline: Megacap split: Apple +1.5% (a day after its intraday record) is the Mag 7 outlier while the MAGS ETF is -1%; Tesla, Meta, Nvidia and Microsoft fell up to 2.5% (Meta -2.1% to $746.62, Microsoft -0.75% to $539.36, per Finnhub). The Data Insights September crowding report: hedge-fund long participation rebounded across Mag 7 (notably Alphabet) while shorts increased in Meta and Tesla — Tesla's long-to-short fund ratio fell to 0.54x, its lowest this year.
headlines.why_it_matters: Rate shocks sell the crowded names first — the positioning data says funds are long the platform (Alphabet) and short the story (Tesla/Meta), which is why the group is trading as a rate proxy, not on company news.
